title: Economic Recovery (Resilience) Team Leader-Roving
description:
The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

Overall purpose of the role: 

The Economic Recovery (Resilience) Team Leader is responsible for the day-to-day technical and operational leadership of DRC's Economic Recovery and resilience programming at field level. The position ensures that activities are appropriately planned, implemented, monitored and reported in line with DRC policies, donor requirements, technical standards and approved project documents.

The position provides technical supervision and guidance to the Economic Recovery field team and supports quality implementation across livelihoods, food security, cash-based assistance, market systems, enterprise development, employment and resilience programming.

The Team Leader ensures that interventions are needs-based, market-oriented, inclusive, conflict-sensitive, accountable to affected populations and responsive to changes in the humanitarian and economic context.

			1. Team Leadership and Supervision

			
				Lead, supervise and mentor Economic Recovery Officers and Assistants.
				Develop and monitor team workplans, priorities and implementation schedules.
				Provide technical guidance, coaching and performance feedback to team members.
				Ensure staff compliance with DRC policies, SOPs, donor requirements, safeguarding and technical standards.
				Identify team capacity gaps and support appropriate training and professional development.
				Ensure effective coordination, delegation and follow-up of field responsibilities.
			

			2. Economic Recovery Programme Implementation

			
				Provide technical leadership for the planning, implementation and monitoring of Economic Recovery and resilience activities.
				Ensure interventions are informed by needs assessments, market and labour-market analysis, community priorities and contextual developments.
				Provide technical oversight across CVA/MPCA, Cash-for-Work, agricultural and livestock livelihoods, vocational skills, BDS/MSME development, financial inclusion, market systems and community resilience activities.
				Ensure programme activities contribute to improved livelihoods, income generation, food security, self-reliance and resilience.
				Promote inclusive programming for women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs, returnees, host communities, pastoralist/nomadic populations and other vulnerable groups.
				Ensure appropriate integration of Economic Recovery activities with other DRC sectors and programmes.
			

			
				Business Development, MSMEs and Market Systems
			

			
				· Provide technical oversight of Business Development Support (BDS), entrepreneurship, MSME and business grant activities.
				· Lead and supervise the field-level implementation of the BDS cycle, including outreach, participant pre-selection, vulnerability and business assessments, Business Management Skills Training (BMST), business planning, pitching, grant implementation, coaching and post-grant monitoring.
				· Ensure business support is based on market assessments, labour-market analysis, business viability, identified economic opportunities and approved project objectives.
				· Ensure BDS participant selection is transparent, inclusive, conflict-sensitive and based on approved eligibility, vulnerability, business potential and market criteria.
				· Review and technically validate business assessments, business plans and grant recommendations before submission through the applicable approval process.
				· Supervise business grant implementation and ensure appropriate follow-up on grant utilization, including verification of business assets, expenditures, supporting documents and compliance with approved business plans and grant agreements.
				· Review and recommend business grant amounts based on business needs, approved business plans, market prices, beneficiary contribution, available budget and applicable donor/project requirements.

title: Protection Officer - RPA/Monitoring
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Protection Officer - RPA/Monitoring for our operations in Negele, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.

Overall purpose of the role:

Under the supervision of the Protection Team Leader the Protection officer (Monitoring), will implement rapid protection assessments (RPA) using KII, FGD and direct observation in operational areas in line with DRC’s protection monitoring SOP. The role holder will also be expected to conduct service mapping and safety audit in operational areas, including protection desks and other humanitarian assistance distribution sites. The position will, furthermore, be tasked to identify and provide direct assistance and support to people with specific needs. The Protection Officer (Monitoring) will ensure referrals of individuals with protection needs, provide information on the available service as part of their RPA and ensure that data collection is in line with protection and humanitarian principles. The officer will also be expected to support drafting the rapid protection analysis.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Develop a work plan for the implementation of rapid protection assessment in the identified locations.
	Ensure rapid protection assessment activities are implemented in line with international standards, best practices and DRC protection monitoring guidelines through KII, FGD and direct observation
	Carry out the RPA activities according to work plan, target and allocated budget
	Contribute to the analysis of the collected information
	Collaborate with the protection manager, IM Officer and Country Office protection technical team, including with the protection specialist for monitoring and analysis in reviewing protection trends and needs in DRC’s areas of intervention and recommend appropriate responses for DRC’s and other agencies
	Conduct service and resource mapping to determine available services and ensure effective protection services and referrals
	Collaborate with relevant partners to develop and maintain protection referral mechanisms.
	Conduct community awareness raising and information dissemination on identified protection risks and prevention and mitigation strategies as well as available services;
	Maintain good professional relationships with other humanitarian partners and stakeholders to collect daily information on protection and support safe referrals
	Mobilize and create strong rapport with communities through engaging with community-based structures on a consistent basis and sticking to respectful, culturally appropriate ways.
	Work with other DRC protection team to encourage referrals and information exchange.
	Ensure ethical and statistically-sound data collection, analysis and protection


Report writing and documentation 


	Develop daily, weekly, monthly report on the RPA and share with protection team leader and protection manager
	Document field level challenges and timely flag for the protection team leader and manager to ensure that challenges are timely communicated and addressed
	Ensure proper documentation of all project activities including means of verification, assessments and case studies.
	Other tasks assigned by the protection team leader/manager.


Experience and technical competencies:


	Minimum of 3 years’ experience in the field of protection and humanitarian response and IDP protection working for an international NGO, UN agency or relevant ministry or local authority.
	Strong communication skills in both English and the local languages; ability to conduct interviews, facilitate discussions, and write reports in English.
	Experience in conducting protection monitoring or protection assessments using online data collection tools such as Kobo and Activity info
	Good data collection, analysis and reporting skills
	Experience working with displaced or conflict affected populations.
	Strong planning, organizational and problem-solving skills with the ability to work both independently and within a team.
	Integrity, strong work ethic, and ability to consistently meet deadlines under pressure.

description:

Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

Overall purpose of the role

Under the supervision of the Support Services Manager/Team Leader, the Human Resources Officer is responsible for delivering efficient HR and administrative services that support DRC operations in the Kordofan Area Office. The role ensures compliance with DRC policies, national labor regulations, and donor requirements, while supporting recruitment, employee lifecycle management, payroll administration, benefits, performance management, and administrative coordination. The position contributes to maintaining a productive, compliant, and people-focused work environment.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Recruitment

Coordinate end-to-end recruitment and selection processes for assigned positions, including vacancy advertisement, hiring manager support, candidate assessment, recruitment tracking, documentation, and preparation of employment contracts, in compliance with DRC recruitment procedures.

Payroll & Staff Records

Maintain accurate and up-to-date employee records in Dynamics, payroll systems, personnel files, and HR SharePoint, ensuring compliance with DRC data management and confidentiality requirements.

National Staff Insurance 

Serve as the focal point for staff health insurance administration, including enrollment, deletions, claims follow-up, card distribution, provider coordination, and submission of payment requests.

Performance Management

Coordinate staff probation, performance appraisal (PADA), and development processes by providing guidance to managers, monitoring completion rates, identifying training needs, and supporting employee development planning.

Audits

Support internal and external audits by maintaining accurate HR documentation and providing required records and reports.

Other Administrative Tasks

Maintain accurate and well-organized administrative records, correspondence, agreements, and supporting documentation in accordance with DRC filing and archiving standards.

Support the implementation and continuous improvement of administrative processes and provide administrative assistance to area operations as required.

Facilities, Accommodation & Asset Administration

Oversee office, guesthouse, and accommodation management, including leases, utilities, maintenance, and visitor support, to ensure safe and functional facilities.

HR Administration & Employee Services

Coordinate staff onboarding and offboarding processes and provide administrative support services to employees in accordance with organizational procedures.

Office Operations & Resource Management

Manage office support services, supplies, and administrative resources to ensure smooth and cost-effective operations.

Overall purpose of the role

To assist in managing safety and liaison activities in Duty Station office and program locations. This includes the compliance adherence to DRC global Safety manual.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Safety


	Assist HoS with the implementation of regional safety policies, safety rules, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) related to the safe implementation of program activities.
	Track access and monitoring of staff field movements to/from duty station.
	Collect, verify, analyze, and submit timely and regular reports on issues that affect, or may affect DRC/HDP operations.

title: Protection Assistant - Monitoring
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a  qualified Protection Assistant – Monitoring  for our operations in our Humera Field Office.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.

Overall purpose of the role 

Under the line management of Protection Team Leader and the technical supervision of the Protection Specialist – Monitoring, the Protection Assistant – Monitoring is responsible for implementing protection monitoring activities in Humera and Maikadra and surrounding areas. The role focuses on conducting regular protection monitoring visits, collecting and encoding data, identifying and referring individuals at risk, sharing information, and reporting on emerging protection risks and trends.

The position will also identify and provide direct assistance to people with specific needs and support the implementation of other protection activities carried out by DRC in the designated project locations.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Conduct protection monitoring in assigned areas
	Contribute in the development and review of protection monitoring tools, testing, plans and in the analysis of the collected information with the Protection Officer and Protection manager.
	Identify and protection trends and needs in the assigned areas through Key Informant Interviews, Focus Group Discussions and observation.
	Utilize data collection system for data collection and uploading in line with international standards, best practices and DRC protection monitoring guidelines
	Identify individuals at risk, provide information and refer for specialized assistance.
	Support coordination and implementation of Individual Protection Assistance.
	Regularly monitor beneficiaries’ access to service, the effectiveness of referral service, and the contribution of referrals and individual protection assistance on addressing protection risks for individual cases.
	Collaborate with Community Based Protection Networks (CBPN) and conduct community awareness raising and information dissemination on identified protection risks and prevention and mitigation strategies.
	Maintain good relationships with CBPNs other stakeholders to collect daily information on fresh displacements in the area of coverage and support safe referrals
	Participate in engaging with community-based structures on a consistent basis and sticking to respectful, culturally appropriate ways.

title: Re-advertisement -Protection Officer – Return, Reintegration & Mixed Migration -P2P
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer

About the job

The Protection Officer is responsible for field-level coordination, implementation and quality assurance of DRC's SIDA P2P protection, return/reintegration and related Economic Recovery linkages in Bosaso and relevant Eastern Route return and transit locations in Puntland. The role supports timely, protection-sensitive delivery of DRC direct activities and field-level accompaniment of local partners across vulnerability screening/case management, PSS, IPA and referrals, route-based Protection Monitoring, reintegration follow-up, livelihoods linkages and systems strengthening.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Protection services, case management and direct assistance


	Coordinate vulnerability screening and protection risk assessment for migrants and returnees and support safe, rights-based case management and referral follow-up in line with DRC SOPs, informed consent, confidentiality and Do No Harm.
	Provide field-level technical guidance to assigned DRC caseworkers and support quality of partner case-management/referral delivery as delegated; ensure GBV, Child Protection, trafficking and other specialized concerns are safely identified and referred.
	Coordinate approved IPA and other immediate protection support, and facilitate safe referrals to MHPSS, health, legal aid, shelter/housing, civil documentation, livelihoods and other specialized services based on assessed needs.


 PSS, return/reintegration and Economic Recovery linkages


	Coordinate/support delivery of structured individual and group PSS and appropriate referral to specialized MHPSS services.
	Support dignified reception, protection screening, information and counselling, access to hotline services, documentation, individualized reintegration planning and structured post-return follow-up, including through the Bosaso MRC and other P2P service points as relevant.
	Work closely with Economic Recovery colleagues and partners to link returnees to market-informed skills, employment/self-employment, business/start-up and financial-inclusion pathways, ensuring protection barriers and safeguarding considerations are integrated.


 Protection Monitoring, referral systems and evidence


	Coordinate regular community and route-based Protection Monitoring in assigned locations; provide day-to-day technical guidance to Protection Monitors/enumerators and ensure urgent protection risks and referral needs trigger appropriate response.
	Support service mapping and referral/RMS strengthening, monitor referral functionality, and contribute to the Ethiopia-Somalia cross-border case-management/legal-aid pilot in line with agreed consent, confidentiality and data-protection protocols.
	Use anonymized Protection Monitoring and referral trends to inform programme adaptation, reporting, validation and evidence/advocacy, keeping confidential case data separate from routine monitoring/MEAL datasets.


 Partner, government and stakeholder coordination


	Provide field-level technical accompaniment to KAALO, participate in joint monitoring with government counterparts and KAALO, and follow up agreed capacity-strengthening actions on Protection, referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and rights-based return/reintegration.
	Support existing government-led migration, referral and reintegration systems through joint monitoring, dialogue, practical coordination and on-the-job support, strengthening rather than creating parallel mechanisms.
	Coordinate with authorities, MRCs, service providers, community structures and humanitarian/protection actors, and support relevant reintegration, social-cohesion and stakeholder-engagement activities as assigned.


 Planning, monitoring, reporting and compliance


	Maintain field activity plans and monitor delivery against approved workplans, budgets, targets and programme-quality standards; identify implementation gaps and support timely corrective action.
	Coordinate with MEAL/IM, Economic Recovery, Partnerships/Grants, Finance and relevant programme/area teams; maintain accurate programme documentation and timely activity/technical reporting.
	Ensure implementation complies with DRC policies and donor requirements, safeguarding/PSEA/AAP commitments, core Protection principles, confidentiality and responsible data management.


About you

To be successful in this role we expect you to have:

Required 


	Minimum 3 years of relevant Protection experience in humanitarian, displacement or mixed-migration settings; experience in return/reintegration is strongly preferred.
	Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, Peace and Conflict Studies, or a closely related field.
	Demonstrated experience in case management/referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and protection-sensitive direct assistance.
	Relevant training in Protect

title: Head of Programme
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Head of Programme for Congo 

Danish Refugee Council is a leading protection agency pursuing our mandate to protect and promote durable solutions to displacement-affected populations based on humanitarian principles. In East Africa and the Great Lakes, DRC has operational presence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda. 

In the DR Congo, DRC has been involved in humanitarian aid since 2009. Initially working in Province Orientale, DRC gradually extended its reach to North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The sectors of intervention for DRC in the country are provision of Emergency Response, Protection (including GBV and child protection), Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH. DRC is currently responding to the Ebola outbreak as this is unfolding in Ituri province where DRC has a longstanding presence.

 

About the job

Provide strategic direction, leadership and oversight of DRC’s country programme, ensuring coherent strategy, high programme quality, effective departmental management and sustainable funding. Lead country-level programme development and support accountable implementation through Area Managers and Project Managers. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the HoP oversees a multi-sector portfolio spanning emergency response, early recovery and resilience in eastern DR Congo, including consortia led by DRC, and works closely with the Head of Support Services and the Head of Safety to balance programme excellence, cost efficiency and safety.

Programme Strategy & Development


	Lead and periodically review the Country Programme Plan, Theory of Change and sector/geographic priorities; translate strategy into clear departmental workplans.
	Coordinate an integrated, multi-sector approach across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; ensure the centrality of protection, safe programming, access and adherence to humanitarian principles; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
	Promote cash and market-based programming (including multi-purpose and emergency cash) and link emergency response with early recovery and durable solutions.
	Drive innovative programme design with the SMT, in line with DRC global and regional strategies.
